text: Joseph could no longer control himself before all who stood attending him, and he called out, "Send everyone away from me!" So no one was with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
He wept aloud, and the Egyptians heard it, and the household of Pharaoh heard it.
Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?" But his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed at his presence.
Then Joseph said to his brothers, "Come closer to me." And they came closer. And he said, "I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
And now, do not be distressed, and do not be angry with yourselves that you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to preserve life.
For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
God sent me ahead of you to preserve for you a remnant in the land and to keep you alive by a great deliverance.

versions.text: God sent me ahead of you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth and to keep you alive by a great deliverance.
versions.explanation: בָּאָרֶץ here most naturally means "in the land" (as in verse 6, where the same word describes the famine's setting); "on the earth" broadens the scope beyond the context.

text: So then, it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord over all his household, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Hurry, go up to my father and say to him, 'This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord over all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.
You shall live in the land of Goshen, and you will be near me—you, your children and your grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and all that you have.
There I will provide for you, for there are five more years of famine, so that you and your household and all that you have will not come to poverty.'
And look, your own eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my own mouth speaking to you.
Tell my father of all my honor in Egypt and of everything you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.
Then he threw his arms around his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

versions.text: Then he threw his arms around his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his shoulder.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses the same word (צַוָּאר, "neck") in both halves of the verse; rendering the second occurrence as "shoulder" loses the deliberate mirroring of the embrace.

text: He kissed all his brothers and wept over them, and afterward his brothers talked with him.
News reached Pharaoh's house: "Joseph's brothers have come." It pleased Pharaoh and his servants.

versions.text: The report was heard in Pharaoh's house: "Joseph's brothers have come." This pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no כֹּל ("all") before "his servants"; the added word is unwarranted.

versions.text: The report was heard in Pharaoh's house: "Joseph's brothers have come." This pleased Pharaoh and his servants.
versions.explanation: The passive "The report was heard in" is stiff for oral reading; "News reached" carries the same sense of הַקֹּל נִשְׁמַע ("the sound/report was heard") with more natural rhythm, and "It pleased" keeps the impersonal Hebrew construction וַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינֵי without the demonstrative "This."

text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers: Do this—load your animals and go back to the land of Canaan.
Get your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
And you are commanded: Do this—take wagons from the land of Egypt for your children and your wives, and bring your father and come.

versions.text: And you are ordered to say this: Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your children and your wives, and bring your father and come.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "you are commanded: do this," with a plural imperative addressed to the brothers; "ordered to say this" inserts an act of speaking that is not in the text and matches the pattern of verse 17 better as "Do this—".

text: Do not worry about your possessions, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours."
So the sons of Israel did this. Joseph gave them wagons, as Pharaoh had commanded, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
To each of them he gave a change of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothes.
And to his father he sent the following: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and provisions for his father's journey.

versions.text: And to his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and food for his father's journey.
versions.explanation: The phrase כְּזֹאת ("the like of this / the following") is left untranslated; including it preserves the introductory formula for the list of gifts.

text: Then he sent his brothers on their way, saying to them, "Do not quarrel on the road."
So they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.
They told him, "Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!" But his heart went numb, for he did not believe them.
Then they told him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.
And Israel said, "Enough! My son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."
